Abstract
With the development of cloud computing framework, the visualization of city 
scenes is shifting to the 3D domain. However, the increase of scene complexity 
makes efficient rendering of virtual city scene an important challenge. To address 
the problem of poor rendering of virtual city scene, the paper proposes an Artificial 
Intelligence (AI) based bundle adjustment point cloud optimization model based 
on cross-entropy loss by combining with the multi-detail hierarchy technique, 
the rendering efficiency is improved while guaranteeing the high consistency 
between the 3D model and the real world in terms of geometry. Comparison of the 
proposed method and model of the study revealed that the F1 value and accuracy 
of the proposed algorithm was 0.87 and 93.9% respectively, which is better than 
the comparison algorithm. Comparison results of the cross-entropy loss-based 
bundle adjustment point cloud optimization model revealed that the output of the 
optimized point cloud model basically focused on − 1 and 1 values instead of fuzzy 
output and showed strong robustness to data containing outliers and noise. The 
virtual city scene rendering experiments revealed that the compression of texture 
data was reduced from the initial 82.5GB to 24.7GB. The optimized virtual city point 
cloud model was able to be fully loaded into memory and video memory at any 
observation point. Time and frame rate experiments revealed that for Scenario 6 
with complex data, the cross-entropy loss-based bundle adjustment point cloud 
optimization model achieved an average frame rate of 495 frames per second. It 
was able to achieve a faster rendering speed while maintaining a lower amount of 
data. The outcomes indicates that this method can effectively enhance the efficient 
rendering performance of virtual city scene and provide useful references and 
lessons for researchers of virtual city scene, to promote the continuous development 
and progress of virtual city scene rendering technology.
Keywords  Cloud computing, Cross-entropy loss function, Bundle adjustment, Point 
cloud optimization, Virtual City scenes, Rendering

1  Introduction
The foundation of building digital and smart cities is urban 3D visualization and simula­
tion technology, which is crucial for vital domains including intelligent transportation, 
virtual geographic information systems, and urban planning [1]. For example, Kikuchi et 
al. developed a digital twin method for outdoor augmented reality using a 3D model of 
the city with first-person view and occlusion processing for bird’s eye view [2]. By lever­
aging new urban data and new technology to meet urban design objectives, Ye et al.‘s 
model for the intelligent rendering of urban master plans through artificial intelligence 
algorithms helps push the methodological frontiers of urban design [3]. Traditional vir­
tual city scene visualization techniques are based on basic data such as satellite remote 
sensing images and regional color maps. The digital presentation usually adopts a two-
dimensional map system, which has the advantage of being able to achieve extensive 
area coverage and multi-scale visualization, while providing efficient data indexing and 
fast spatial data retrieval [4 and [5]. However, 2D orthographic projections have limita­
tions and users can only obtain a limited depth of information [6].
With the development of cloud computing frameworks, the visualization of urban 
scenes is shifting to the 3D domain, aiming to provide more detailed information and 
a more realistic visual experience [7]. Hu et al. presented a collaborative adaptive cruise 
control (CACC) simulation platform designed for urban environments. This platform 
might be integrated into the development of autonomous and networked vehicle control 
systems. It was possible to measure the safety of CACC control in urban settings, assess 
different traffic regulations for CACC control, and record the interactions between 
human-driven cars and self-driving auto control systems [8]. To aid in semantic segmen­
tation in dimly lit urban situations, Zhou et al. suggested a novel semantic segmentation 
network called MMSMCNet, which is based on modal memory fusion and morphologi­
cal multiscale assistance [9]. However, with the increase of scene complexity, it becomes 
a great challenge to render virtual city scene efficiently. The virtual city scene usually 
contains a large amount of geometric data, texture mapping and lighting effects, etc., 
which puts extreme demands on the rendering performance [10]. Traditional rendering 
methods often suffer from slow rendering speed, frame rate degradation, lag, etc. when 
facing large-scale and highly detailed virtual city scene, which seriously affects the user’s 
experiential effect [11]. Under the cloud computing framework, the data-driven point 
cloud optimization strategy improves the rendering efficiency and performance of the 
virtual city scene by leveraging the powerful computing power and scalability of cloud 
computing to efficiently process and optimize large-scale point cloud data (PCD). The 
bundle adjustment (BA) technique works through collaborative strategies and technical 
means to fine-tune and optimize various aspects of the rendering process to optimize 
the point cloud model (PCM) and improve the rendering performance. For the large-
scale virtual city scene, the study proposes a BA algorithm based on cross-entropy loss 
(CL) for intelligent partitioning and layering of the scene. Meanwhile, level of detail 
(LOD) technique is utilized to dynamically adjust the fineness of the model accord­
ing to the distance and importance of objects in the scene. The rendering efficiency is 
further improved while guaranteeing the high geometric consistency between the 3D 
model and the real world. The innovation of the research is mainly reflected in the fol­
lowing two points. Firstly, by utilizing the powerful computing power and scalability of 
cloud computing, the performance bottleneck problem encountered by the traditional

rendering methods when dealing with large-scale and high-detail scenes is effectively 
solved. Second, the rendering performance is further improved by intelligently partition­

ing the model fineness according to the distance and importance of objects in the scene 
by combining with the LOD technique. This provides useful references and lessons for

2  Data-driven point cloud optimization strategy based on CL-BA algorithm
2.1  Introduction of the BA algorithm for CL
Under the framework of cloud computing, data-driven approaches have become an 
effective way to render virtual city scene, which provides great convenience for the 
visualization of urban scenes [12]. However, the accumulation of errors in the data pro­
cessing process may lead to significant differences in the geometrical form between the 
PCM and the actual scene [13]. To obtain more accurate models, it becomes crucial to 
optimize the PCD, and the BA technique has thus received extensive attention from 
researchers at home and abroad. The BA technique analyzes image data captured by 
multiple cameras from different viewpoints by minimizing the projection error of fea­
ture points on the imaging plane. It also optimizes the internal and external parameters 
of the cameras and the positions of 3D points in the scene to achieve accurate modeling 
of the scene, as shown in Fig. 1 [14].
In Fig. 1, the BA technique is mainly realized through a dynamic optimization pro­
cess. The dynamic optimization process involves the continuous adjustment of camera 
parameters and point coordinates in 3D space. This reduces the disparity between the 
observed points in the image and the projected points obtained from the 3D model’s 
projection, thereby improving the scene model’s geometric accuracy. Consequently, 
throughout the dynamic optimization process, particular attention must be given to

2.2  Point cloud optimization strategy for virtual scene rendering performance 
improvement
The study is conducted after optimizing the PCM by BA technique. To further enhance 
the rendering performance, on the basis of the optimized PCM by BA technique, a 
data rendering model is also needed for further PCM optimization. The data render­
ing model is based on a dynamic multi-element rendering strategy that dynamically ren­
ders 3D forms by intelligently selecting combinations of point-line and polygonal images 
based on the size of the rasterized area on the screen [23]. For architectural objects, the 
edge contours are outlined by line rendering techniques, while the surfaces are repre­
sented in detail by a dynamically adjustable number of point tuples. When the observer’s 
viewpoint is far away, the rendering of the 3D model is simplified and represented by a 
small number of points and line segments for efficient approximate rendering. When the 
observer is close to the object, the rendering details will be enhanced with point and line 
blending and incorporating procedural texturing techniques to enrich the visual effect. 
It may dynamically modify the model’s rendering details at various viewing distances, 
ensuring rendering efficiency and satisfying the need for varied visual effects. The data 
rendering model firstly needs to sample the point pixels, which are used to generate the 
point-based 3D model. The sampling of the point-element is shown in Fig. 4.
In Fig.  4, the data rendering model first performs multi-layer meshing and subse­
quently performs point sampling on these meshes to ensure that sampled points in the 
same layer are not duplicated in rows or columns of the mesh to achieve a random dis­
tribution. The N-rooks sampling rule is shown in Eq. (11).

3  Experimental results and analysis
3.1  Comparative performance analysis of CL-BA algorithm
To analyze the performance of the CL-BA algorithm proposed in the study, the study 
conducted a comparison experiment with KL-BA algorithm and BA algorithm. The 
experiment was conducted in the following environment to ensure the repeatability and 


Page 11 of 20
Zhongda Discover Computing          (2025) 28:146 
reliability of the experimental results. First, the experimental equipment is a desktop 
computer equipped with Intel Xeon E5-2620 processor and NVidia GTX 480 graphics 
card. The device provides powerful computing power and graphics rendering capabili­
ties to meet the needs of large-scale point cloud processing and 3D scene rendering. In 
addition, the operating system adopts CentOS 7, the programming language is Python, 
and the open-source libraries such as OpenCV and PCL are used for image process­
ing and Point Cloud processing. Finally, we study the use of PyCharm as an integrated 
development environment to facilitate code writing, debugging, and management. The 
experimental data sets include BAL data set and city-level 3D scene data set. BAL data 
set is used to evaluate the performance and accuracy of CL-BA algorithm, and city-level 
3D scene data set is used to verify the rendering effect of the algorithm in real scenes.
To ensure a fair comparison, the three models use the same parameter Settings and 
data preprocessing steps. Data preprocessing mainly includes the following steps. First, 
noise removal and outlier detection are carried out on the original point cloud data. 
The noise points are identified and eliminated by statistical analysis and median filter­
ing technology. Outliers are processed by threshold judgment or density-based cluster­
ing methods. After that, the original point cloud data is converted from the acquisition 
device coordinate system to the global coordinate system to ensure that point cloud 
data from different perspectives and sources can be processed under a unified spatial 
framework. The global point cloud data is then divided into multiple grids for subse­
quent point sampling and level of detail adjustment. The size and shape of the grid are 
set according to the scene complexity and rendering requirements. Finally, within each 
grid, point sampling is performed according to a random sampling strategy to reduce 
data size and retain key features.
In addition, the main parameters of CL-BA are set as follows, weight of loss function: 
In the cross-entropy loss function, weights of different classes can be set to deal with 
class imbalance. For a few categories, the weight is set to 2.0, and for most categories, the 
weight remains 1.0. The LM algorithm parameters are set as follows: The damping factor 
(λ) is the key parameter for balancing the convergence rate of gradient descent and New­
ton method, and its initial value is set to 0.001, which is dynamically adjusted accord­
ing to the convergence of the optimization process. For example, if the convergence 
rate is too slow, λ is reduced, If the oscillation increases λ. In the dynamic multi-pixel 
rendering strategy, the detail level threshold is set under different distance and impor­
tance to determine the detail level of different rendering levels. When the observer is 
less than 10 m away from the object, the highest level of detail is used (100 sampling 
points per meter); When the observer is between 10 and 100 m away from the object, 
use a medium level of detail (50 sampling points per meter); When the observer is more 
than 100 m away from the object, the lowest level of detail is used (10 sampling points 
per meter). By contrasting the three algorithms’ error, accuracy, and other performance 
metrics, the three algorithms are evaluated. Figure 8 displays the error results for the 
three algorithms in the training and test sets.
In Fig. 8(a), the CL-BA algorithm has the lowest training error of 0.051 and 0.046 in 
the test and training set, respectively. In Fig. 6(b), the KL-BA algorithm has the lowest 
training error of 0.075 and 0.083 in the test and training set, respectively. In Fig. 6(c), the 
BA algorithm has the lowest training error of 0.103 and 0.127 in the test and training 
sets, respectively. The findings indicates that the suggested CL-BA algorithm has a lower

3.2  Performance test of point cloud optimization model based on CL-BA algorithm
To verify the accuracy and efficiency of the point cloud optimization model based on 
the CL-BA algorithm even further, the study chooses the BAL dataset to assess the 
point cloud optimization model’s time efficiency and accuracy. Moreover, the developed 
model is compared with general graph optimization (g2o) and sparse suite for bundle 
adjustment (sSBA) models to show its superiority in classification accuracy and effi­

4  Discussion
The proposed CL-BA algorithm shows remarkable advantages in the performance com­
parison experiment. In terms of error, accuracy, F1 value and other dimensions, CL-BA 
algorithm is superior to KL-BA algorithm and original BA algorithm. Especially when 
dealing with large-scale data sets, CL-BA algorithm can maintain low error level and 
high accuracy, which is mainly due to its optimized algorithm design and stronger data 
processing ability. This result is similar to the conclusion obtained by Ozdoba’s study in 
2022 [26]. In addition, the point cloud optimization model based on CL-BA algorithm 
also shows strong robustness when dealing with data containing outliers and noise, 
which further proves the reliability and practicability of the algorithm. In the perfor­
mance test of point cloud optimization model, CL-BA algorithm also shows excellent 
performance. Compared with g2o and sSBA models, CL-BA algorithm not only has 
shorter iteration time when processing large-scale data sets but also has more accurate 
and clear output results. This is mainly due to the high efficiency and accuracy of CL-BA 
algorithm in the optimization process, so that it can get more accurate results in a short 
time. The above results coincide with those obtained by Kaplan when testing the point 
cloud optimization algorithm [27].
In the empirical analysis for virtual city rendering, the point cloud optimization model 
based on CL-BA algorithm also shows significant advantages. In terms of rendering time, 
frame rate and visual effect, CL-BA model is superior to traditional triangular mesh ren­
dering and GLOD model. This is mainly because the CL-BA algorithm can dynamically 
adjust the number of rendering primitives according to the user’s viewing distance, so as 
to achieve a balance between the visual effect and performance of the scene under differ­
ent resolutions and viewing distance conditions. Compared with the relevant research, 
the CL-BA algorithm proposed in this study has significantly improved its performance. 
For example, compared with the algorithm proposed by Shen’s team, the proposed algo­
rithm shows stronger advantages and practicability when processing large-scale data 
sets and data containing outliers and noise [28]. In addition, compared with the virtual 
city rendering model proposed by Long et al., the proposed point cloud optimization 
model based on CL-BA algorithm also shows significant advantages in virtual city ren­
dering, providing a new and more efficient method for the construction and rendering of 
virtual cities [29].
The research contributions are mainly reflected in the following three aspects: First, 
a new CL-BA algorithm with excellent performance is proposed; Secondly, an efficient 
point cloud optimization model is constructed based on CL-BA algorithm. Thirdly, 
CL-BA algorithm and point cloud optimization model are successfully applied to virtual 
city rendering, and remarkable results are achieved. These contributions not only pro­
vide new ideas and methods for research in related fields but also provide strong support 
and guarantee for practical applications.
5  Conclusion
Traditional rendering methods often suffer from slow rendering speed, frame rate deg­
radation, lagging and other problems when facing large-scale and highly detailed virtual 
city scene, which seriously affects the user’s experience effect. To address this problem, 
the study proposes a point cloud optimization model based on the BA algorithm of CL 
for intelligent partitioning and layering of the scene. At the same time, LOD technology

is utilized to dynamically adjust the fineness of the model according to the distance and 
importance of objects in the scene. The rendering efficiency is further improved while 
guaranteeing a high degree of geometric consistency between the 3D model and the real 
world. The validation experiments on the effectiveness of the CL LF indicated that the 
CL LF had great advantages in improving the accuracy of the model, and its robustness 
was superior to other LFs. The virtual city scene rendering experiments revealed that the 
virtual city PCM optimized by the CL-BA algorithm could be completely loaded into 
the storage under any observation point. The detail level of the model was dynamically 
adjusted according to the distance of the observation points from the data clusters, and 
it was able to be rendered at a rate of 42 to 51 frames per second on the testbed. The 
rendering time and frame rate experiments revealed that the point cloud optimization 
model based on CL-BA algorithm proposed in the study had significant advantages in 
terms of rendering time. Its rendering times in all scenes were 45ms, 40ms, 57ms, 36ms, 
43ms, and 49ms, respectively, which were much lower than the triangular mesh render­
ing and GLOD models. In consideration of image quality and visual continuity, the point 
cloud optimization model, based on the CL-BA algorithm, is capable of dynamically 
adjusting the rendering strategy in accordance with varying resolutions and viewing 
distances, thereby enhancing the rendering efficiency. Based on the research focusing 
on virtual city rendering performance optimization, the future exploration will deeply 
expand to the multi-dimensional representation of city visualization. In addition to 
enhancing the fundamental rendering efficiency, the objective is to integrate a diversified 
data set, including information such as noise distribution and air pollutant concentra­
tion, to construct a more comprehensive and information-rich urban visualization.

Abstract: With the development of cloud computing framework, the visualization of city scenes is shifting to the 3D domain. However, the increase of scene complexity makes efficient rendering of virtual city scene an important challenge. To address the problem of poor rendering of virtual city scene, the paper proposes an Artificial Intelligence (AI) based bundle adjustment point cloud optimization model based on cross-entropy loss by combining with the multi-detail hierarchy technique, the rendering efficiency is improved while guaranteeing the high consistency between the 3D model and the real world in terms of geometry. Comparison of the proposed method and model of the study revealed that the F1 value and accuracy of the proposed algorithm was 0.87 and 93.9% respectively, which is better than the comparison algorithm. Comparison results of the cross-entropy loss-based bundle adjustment point cloud optimization model revealed that the output of the optimized point cloud model basically focused on − 1 and 1 values instead of fuzzy output and showed strong robustness to data containing outliers and noise. The virtual city scene rendering experiments revealed that the compression of texture data was reduced from the initial 82.5GB to 24.7GB. The optimized virtual city point cloud model was able to be fully loaded into memory and video memory at any observation point. Time and frame rate experiments revealed that for Scenario 6 with complex data, the cross-entropy loss-based bundle adjustment point cloud optimization model achieved an average frame rate of 495 frames per second. It was able to achieve a faster rendering speed while maintaining a lower amount of data. The outcomes indicates that this method can effectively enhance the efficient rendering performance of virtual city scene and provide useful references and lessons for researchers of virtual city scene, to promote the continuous development and progress of virtual city scene rendering technology.
